newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi oil flows to Turkey in earnest.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi oil flows to Turkey in earnest.

text.p: The first Iraqi oil to flow to world markets in six years began in earnest Wednesday under the "oil-for-food" deal that Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's government reached with the United Nations.
A Turkish pipeline official said oil from Iraq began flowing around midday and he expected about 350,000 barrels a day to be pumped to Turkey's Ceyhan port from the Iraqi oil city of Kirkuk.
Turkish oil officials said the first oil would probably leave Ceyhan over the weekend.
Iraq said an earlier technical problem that disrupted shipments Tuesday had been quickly solved.

Saddam pushed a button Tuesday to release the first of $2 billion worth of oil Baghdad is allowed to sell in the next six months. But only a negligible amount had trickled into Turkey until Wednesday.
In Baghdad, an official at Iraq's oil ministry said a technical problem had held up the flow of crude for a short time but Iraqi technicians solved it.
Most revenue from the U.N.-approved plan are to go toward humanitarian aid for Iraqis suffering under economic sanctions imposed after Iraq invaded Kuwait.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said the flow of Iraqi oil to Turkey was now not facing any political or technical problems.
The minister blamed earlier reports that Iraqi oil shipments were stalled on those "whose aim was to undermine the gains of the Iraqi people," the official Iraqi news agency INA reported.
